t: Aim and plan of the session
n: In this session we study the toxicological significance and the methods of analysis of derivatives of synthetic pyrethroids. The aim is to familiarise students with this topic. The plan has three stages. First, the toxicological significance of pyrethroids. Second, methods of isolating and analysing cypermethrin, danitol and decis. Third, a situational problem. The topic of the session is devoted to isolating these substances from objects and analysing them.

By the end of the session, students master the conditions for carrying out qualitative reactions both in pure solutions and in a solution of unknown composition. For this, test tubes, separating funnels, reagents and visual aids will be needed. The work is carried out in a room equipped with special laboratory facilities. That is, we study theory together with practical work.

We begin with the safety rules. For the laboratory work the student brings rubber gloves, a wipe and a face mask. The examination is carried out in rooms with ventilation and a fume cupboard. Such rooms are locked and sealed when the work is finished. Objects from infected persons, that is those with tuberculosis, hepatitis and AIDS, arrive in a special container and are noted in the documents.

Let us dwell on the significance of synthetic pyrethroids. Synthetic pyrethroid pesticides produced at the Navoi Electrochemical Plant have not been sufficiently studied from the chemical-toxicological point of view. They are distinguished by high efficacy, use in small amounts and broad action on diverse species of insects. High toxicity, LD50=50-400 mg/kg, and wide use have caused poisoning of people and animals. The lack of diagnostic methods and of validated methods of analysis in biological fluids and physical evidence is one of the causes leading to death.

Now the representatives of synthetic pyrethroids. This group includes danitol, cypermethrin, decis, karate, sumi-alpha and other representatives. The trade names of cypermethrin are ripcord, arrivo and cymbush. Decis is also known under the names deltamethrin, butox and K-othrine. Danitol is also called fenpropathrin. In Uzbekistan it is produced under the name Uzfen. Remember: one substance may occur under several names.

Danitol, that is fenpropathrin, is an ester of 2,2,3,3-tetramethylcyclopropanecarboxylic acid and α-cyano-3-phenoxybenzyl alcohol. It is a white crystalline powder. The melting point is 45-50 °C, and it is practically insoluble in water; its solubility at 20 °C is 0.34 mg/l. It dissolves in methanol, hexane, acetone, chloroform and dimethylformamide. Do not forget either that it is stable to light and heating.

The toxicological significance of danitol is great. It is highly toxic: the oral LD50 is 49-54 for rats, 58-67 for mice and 1089 mg/kg for ducks. It is extremely toxic to aquatic animals: for fish the LC50 in 24 hours is 2.2-9.6 µg/l. In Uzbekistan it is produced under the name Uzfen as a 20% emulsion concentrate. It is used against cotton bollworms, mites and moths.

Danitol in figures. The melting point of the white crystalline powder is 45-50 °C. In water at 20 °C, 0.34 mg/l dissolves. The oral LD50 is 49-54 for rats, 58-67 for mice and 1089 mg/kg for ducks. For fish the LC50 in 24 hours is 2.2-9.6 µg/l. These figures show that the substance is especially dangerous to aquatic animals.

Cypermethrin, that is ripcord, arrivo, cymbush, is a mixture of cis and trans isomers. The cis isomer is 40% and the trans isomer 60%. It is a yellowish oily liquid with a faint smell. The technical product, containing 90% of the main substance, is a dark brown oily liquid, non-volatile. It is practically insoluble in water, with a solubility of 0.03 mg/l. Under strongly alkaline conditions it undergoes hydrolysis; in an aqueous medium at pH 5-7 it is stable. Density at 25 °C is 1.23 g/cm3. It dissolves well in acetone, xylene, chloroform and cyclohexane; it mixes with alcohol, ketone, organochlorine and aromatic hydrocarbons.

Toxicological significance of cypermethrin. It is highly toxic: the oral LD50 is 200-415 for rats and 63 mg/kg for mice. It is not toxic to birds, but acts strongly on bees. For fish the LD50 in 96 hours is 0.0012 mg/l. The permissible amount in food products is 2.0-0.1 mg/kg. It is used against the cotton bollworm, Colorado beetle, thrips and others at a volume of 0.1-1.0 l/ha.

Cypermethrin in figures. The cis isomer makes up 40% and the trans isomer 60%. The technical product contains 90% of the main substance. It is practically insoluble in water, with a solubility of 0.03 mg/l. Density at 25 °C is 1.23 g/cm3. In an aqueous medium, at pH 5-7, it is stable. The LD50 is 200-415 for rats and 63 mg/kg for mice. That is, for mice this substance is considerably more toxic.

Decis, that is deltamethrin, butox, K-othrine, is a white crystalline substance. The melting point is 98-101 °C. It is practically insoluble in water: 0.002 mg/l at 20 °C. It dissolves in acetone, benzene, dimethyl sulfoxide, cyclohexanone and dioxane, and is stable under acidic conditions. Production forms: 2.5% emulsion concentrate, dust, granules and 0.5% ULV solutions.

Let us compare the three substances. Danitol is a white crystalline powder with a melting point of 45-50 °C. Cypermethrin is an oily liquid, a mixture of 40% cis and 60% trans isomers. Decis is a white crystalline substance with a melting point of 98-101 °C. LD50 for rats: danitol 49-54, decis 128.5-138.7, cypermethrin 200-415 mg/kg. All three are highly toxic to bees and fish.

Toxicological significance of decis. It is highly toxic to warm-blooded animals: the LD50 is 128.5-138.7 for rats and 300 mg/kg for dogs. It has an irritant effect on the skin and mucous membranes, and accumulates in the body in small amounts. It is also highly toxic to bees and fish. The permissible amount is 0.006 mg/l in domestic water bodies and 0.01 mg/kg in soil.

Decis in figures. The melting point of deltamethrin is 98-101 °C. In water at 20 °C, 0.002 mg/l dissolves. The LD50 is 128.5-138.7 for rats and 300 mg/kg for dogs. The permissible amount in domestic water bodies is 0.006 mg/l, in soil 0.01 mg/kg. These values serve as the basis in assessing the substance.

Now we turn to the methods of isolation. First, isolating pyrethroids from blood. 5 ml of blood is taken, and the pH is brought to 8-9 with NaOH. Then 2 ml of saturated NaCl and 10 ml of organic solvent are added. The mixture is centrifuged for 5 minutes and the organic layer is separated. The process is repeated twice more. The isolates are combined and filtered, and the solvent is evaporated. The dry residue is examined by TLC, HPLC and UV.

Let us compare the conditions of isolation from blood, urine and tissue. Blood: 5 ml sample, pH 8-9, 2 ml saturated NaCl, 10 ml organic solvent, 5 minutes of centrifugation. Urine: 25 ml, 3 g NaCl, pH 8-9; extraction with 30, 20, 20 ml of solvent. Tissue: 10 g of object, pH 9.0-9.5, 15 ml of solvent and 5 ml of saturated NaCl, shaken for 1 hour. As you see, the pH is slightly higher for tissue.

Isolating pyrethroids from urine. 3 g of NaCl is added to 25 ml of urine. The pH is brought to 8-9 with 0.1 M NaOH. Extraction is carried out 3 times, that is with 30, 20 and 20 ml. The isolate is passed through a filter with Na2SO4, and the filter is washed with 5 ml of solvent. The solvent is distilled off in a rotary vacuum evaporator until 0.5 ml remains. The residue is dried and examined.

t: Isolating pyrethroids from a biological object
n: Isolating pyrethroids from a biological object. 10 g of the minced object is mixed with 1-3 ml of water and brought to pH 9.0-9.5 with 0.1 M NaOH. Then 15 ml of solvent and 5 ml of saturated NaCl are added and shaken for 1 hour on a shaker. The extraction is repeated 2 more times. The isolates are passed through a filter with Na2SO4. The solvent is distilled off in a rotary vacuum evaporator, and the residue is dried and examined.

t: Degree of extraction: urine, blood, tissue
n: The degree of extraction differs depending on the object. When cypermethrin and decis are isolated with chloroform, and danitol with ethyl acetate, the highest degree is obtained from urine. For cypermethrin, 79.50 per cent in urine, 75.66 in blood, 50.54 in tissue. For danitol, 78.30, 67.20 and 50.00. For decis, 78.56, 77.60 and 51.46. From biological material, that is tissue, the degree of extraction is about 50%. Danitol is isolated from blood with hexane-ethyl acetate, 1:1, at 67.20%.

Methods of analysis have been developed: TLC, GLC, HPLC, GC-MS and UV spectrophotometry. In thin-layer chromatography, the plates are chosen according to the substance. For danitol, Silufol, that is Silpearl sorbent, is used. For cypermethrin, silica gel LS 5/40 µm prepared in the laboratory. For sumi-alpha, decis and karate, Sorbfil plates: STKh-1VE, particles 8-12 µm, and STKh-1A, 5-17 µm.

t: Analytical methods for pyrethroids and plates
n: Let us list the methods of analysis. For analysis, TLC, GLC, HPLC, GC-MS and UV spectrophotometry have been developed. For danitol, Silufol is used; for cypermethrin, a silica gel plate prepared in the laboratory. For sumi-alpha, decis and karate, Silufol and Sorbfil plates are used. In GLC, the SE-30 sorbent is used, in HPLC a C-18 column, and in UV spectrophotometry the region of 260-280 nm.

Developing reagents and detection limits in TLC. With a 0.5% aqueous solution of bromophenol blue the detection limit is 2.5 µg, for sumi-alpha, decis and karate. For danitol, Marquis reagent, limit 2 µg. For cypermethrin, chlorine-zinc-iodine, limit 1.5 µg, and Dragendorff reagent modified according to Munier, limit 2 µg. For sumi-alpha, decis and karate, a 1% aqueous solution of sodium eosinate, limit 2 µg.

Let us look at the detection limits once more. With chlorine-zinc-iodine the limit is 1.5 µg. Dragendorff according to Munier 2 µg. The detection limit of danitol with Marquis reagent is 2 µg. With a 1% solution of sodium eosinate the limit is 2 µg. With a 0.5% solution of bromophenol blue 2.5 µg. It can be seen that the most sensitive reagent is chlorine-zinc-iodine.

For cypermethrin in TLC, three systems are recommended, with the Rf values given correspondingly. Hexane and acetone, in the ratio 5:1, Rf 0.44. Chloroform and methanol, 7:1, Rf 0.58. Hexane and ethyl acetate, 3:1, Rf 0.61. Remember: an Rf has meaning only together with its own system.

Systems for other pyrethroids. Sumi-alpha: hexane and chloroform, 2:1, Rf 0.68. Karate: chloroform and hexane, 2:1, Rf 0.57. For danitol, hexane and acetone, 2:1, Rf 0.55; hexane and ethyl acetate, 3:1, Rf 0.47. For decis, chloroform and hexane, 3:2, Rf 0.6. For each substance the system and the Rf value are recorded together.

GLC conditions. The column is glass, 130x0.2 cm. The sorbent is 5% SE-30 impregnated on the surface of Chromaton N-AW-DMCS. The mobile phase is nitrogen, 30 ml/min; hydrogen 30 ml/min, air 350 ml/min. The oven is heated from 180 to 220 °C at 1 °C/min, then to 245 °C at 3 °C/min. Detector temperature 260, injector 250 °C.

Instrument and column for HPLC. The instrument is an Agilent Technologies Agilent 1100 series chromatograph, controlled by the Chemstation A.09.03 program. It has a four-channel gradient pump, a degasser and a UV-VIS spectrophotometric detector of 190-600 nm. The column is Zorbax Eclipse XDB C-18, 150x3 mm, particles 3.5 µm. Pyrethroids are analysed at 278-280 nm.

The mobile phase in HPLC. It consists of phosphate buffer at pH=3.0, A, and acetonitrile, B, and works in gradient mode. The flow is 0.5 ml/min. At the beginning, at 0 minutes, A 80%, B 20%. At 7-20 minutes, A 25%, B 75%. At 24 minutes, again A 80%, B 20%. The duration of the analysis is 24 minutes.

Retention times in HPLC. Danitol elutes at 17.4 minutes. The cypermethrin isomers at 18.7 and 19.7 minutes, decis at 20.1, sumi-alpha at 20.9 minutes. The retention time of karate is 21.9 minutes. Because cypermethrin consists of two isomers, it gives two peaks.

The order in which the substances elute. The duration of the analysis is 24 minutes. Danitol elutes first, with a retention time of 17.4 minutes. Then the cypermethrin isomers, 18.7 and 19.7. Then decis at 20.1, sumi-alpha at 20.9, and last of all karate at 21.9 minutes.

UV spectrophotometry. The UV spectrum is measured at a layer thickness of 10 mm in the wavelength range of 200-400 nm. Suitable organic solvents are used as the reference solution. Pesticides absorb with one maximum each in the region of 260-280 nm. That is, one characteristic peak is observed in the spectrum.

Let us sum up the UV spectrophotometry conditions. Layer thickness 10 mm. Measurement range 200-400 nm. Pesticides have the property of absorbing with one maximum each in the region of 260-280 nm. This region serves as the basis for recognising the substance.

Situational problem: pyrethroid or carbamate? The internal organs of the corpse of X. U., born 1952, were submitted to the forensic chemistry department. In jar No. 1, 200 g of stomach; in jar No. 2, 300 g of large and small intestine, and a piece of lung. When the object was opened, a sharp smell of carbamic acid was perceived. Circumstances: at home, while treating potatoes and tomatoes, his health deteriorated and he died. In the preliminary analysis, when the dry residue obtained from the chloroform isolate is viewed under the microscope, crystals in the shape of (+) form.

Scheme of pyrethroid analysis. Depending on the object, extraction with an organic solvent is carried out at pH 8-9, for blood and urine, or 9.0-9.5, for tissue. The dry residue is examined by TLC, HPLC and UV; there are also GLC and GC-MS methods. In TLC, the plate, system and developing reagent suited to the type of substance are chosen. The Rf is compared with the witness. Finally the result is interpreted.

Interpreting the result and limitations. An Rf value has meaning only together with the corresponding system, plate and reagent, for example danitol: hexane-acetone 2:1, Rf 0.55. The detection limits are 1.5-2.5 µg: a smaller amount may not be visible in TLC. Because cypermethrin is a mixture of isomers, two peaks are expected in HPLC, at 18.7 and 19.7 minutes. The lack of validated methods makes the diagnosis of pyrethroid poisoning difficult.
Application rates. Danitol is used on cotton fields at 1.0-2.0 l/ha. Plants can be treated up to four times. Cypermethrin is used at a volume of 0.1-1.0 l/ha, and decis at 0.1-3.0 l/ha.

Permissible amounts. The tentative safe exposure level of cypermethrin is 0.006 mg/l for the aquatic environment and 0.02 mg/kg for soil. The permissible amount of decis in domestic water bodies is 0.006 mg/l, and in soil 0.01 mg/kg. That is, for water the norm of both substances is the same, while for soil it differs.

Review questions. First: on what basis are toxic chemicals divided into classes in toxicological chemistry, and write their formulae. Second: by what methods are synthetic pyrethroids isolated from an object, which is preferable, and what is the significance of pH, the nature of the solvent and the number of soakings. Third: the purposes of isolating cypermethrin, danitol and decis, purification from foreign substances, preliminary approximate analysis, and reactions establishing authenticity. Fourth: on what are the general and specific methods of quantifying pyrethroids based, and how are chemicals containing pyrethroids isolated from an object and analysed.

Conclusion. Pyrethroids are isolated from blood and urine at pH 8-9, and from tissue at pH 9.0-9.5, with an organic solvent. In TLC, cypermethrin Rf 0.44, 0.58, 0.61; danitol 0.55 and 0.47; sumi-alpha 0.68, karate 0.57, decis 0.6. In HPLC, analysis is at 278-280 nm. Retention times: danitol 17.4, cypermethrin 18.7 and 19.7, decis 20.1, sumi-alpha 20.9, karate 21.9 minutes.
